topic: How does a battery light a bulb?
title: How does a battery actually light a bulb?
description:
A battery does not send electricity out like water in a pipe. It pushes electrons around a closed loop, and they heat a thin filament until it glows. See the whole loop, and what happens inside the bulb.

#science #electricity #physics #howitworks #shorts

beats.sentence: How does a battery light a bulb?
beats.subject: battery
beats.change: the charge window fills and turns from red to green

beats.subject: battery
beats.change: the charge window glows brighter green as the battery fills

beats.sentence: The battery pushes electrons around a closed loop of wire.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: glowing dots begin to flow around the closed loop of wire

beats.sentence: Inside the battery, a chemical reaction piles extra electrons onto the negative end.
beats.subject: particles
beats.change: dots crowd together and pile up at the negative end of the battery

beats.sentence: Those crowded electrons shove away from each other and flow out along one wire.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the dots spread apart and stream out along the wire from the battery to the bulb

beats.sentence: They travel through the bulb, then back along the other wire to the positive end.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the dots pass through the bulb and stream back along the other wire to the battery

beats.sentence: The wire was already full of electrons, so the whole line moves at once.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: every dot along the whole loop starts moving together at the same moment

beats.sentence: Each electron drifts slowly, only a fraction of a millimetre every second.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the dots slow down to a gentle crawl while the bulb glow stays on

beats.subject: lightbulb
beats.change: the bulb switches on and its glass starts to glow warm

beats.sentence: Its thin tungsten filament is a very narrow path.
beats.subject: lightbulb
beats.change: the filament lights up and electrons line up to enter it inside the glass

beats.sentence: Electrons squeeze through it and crash into the metal atoms.
beats.subject: particles
beats.change: electrons squeeze into the filament and bump into the atoms there

beats.sentence: Every crash makes the atoms jiggle faster.
beats.subject: particles
beats.change: the atoms in the filament jiggle faster and turn from orange to red

beats.sentence: The filament heats up to about two thousand degrees Celsius.
beats.subject: thermometer
beats.change: the liquid rises and turns from blue to red

beats.sentence: At that heat, the glowing metal gives off bright white light.
beats.subject: lightbulb
beats.change: the filament glows from red to bright white and the glass lights up

beats.sentence: Think of a crowd squeezing through a narrow gate, jostling as they go.
beats.subject: crowd
beats.change: the tiny people pack together and squeeze through the narrow gap

beats.sentence: Cut the loop anywhere and the flow stops, so the light goes out.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the loop breaks, the dots stop moving and the bulb fades dark

beats.sentence: That is why a switch works.
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the gap closes, the dots start moving again and the bulb relights

beats.sentence: If you broke the wire, where would the electrons stop?
beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the wire splits open and the dots bunch up on both sides of the gap

beats.subject: wire
beats.change: the gap glows as the dots pile up at its edges
